constraint: Two markets can carry dedicated GTM capacity over the next four quarters; the rest get coverage at best.

criteria.rationale: The constraint is four quarters, so a market with live mandates and budget beats a larger market that is still forming an opinion.
The ICP is unusually sharp (a data constraint plus a security veto), and markets that do not have that constraint default to the hyperscaler no matter what we do.
This ICP buys through analysts, partners, and procurement, so an existing route in is worth more than it would be in a self-serve motion.
Weighted below readiness because the specialist position is only defensible where the gate exists; where it does not, position is irrelevant.
Low weight on purpose: nearly every market on this slate is enterprise-sized, so it barely discriminates.
Inverted, and modest, because regulation usually creates our demand rather than blocking it; it only matters where a regime is one we cannot yet meet.

knockouts.desc: Market entry controlled by an exclusive competitor arrangement

markets.name: Canadian public sector

evidence.value: Federal partnership agreement on public-service AI, plus up to $240M sovereign compute investment
Sovereignty and in-country data requirements are structural, not preferences

markets.notes: The existing federal relationship is coverage, not saturation: provinces, agencies, and crown corporations are largely unworked.

markets.name: Canadian financial services

evidence.value: Every Big Five bank has a public GenAI program; CIBC platform enterprise-wide, TD targeting $1B AI value, Manulife GenAI to 100 percent of staff
Strong in-house AI capability at several banks (Layer 6 at TD) and hyperscaler incumbency

markets.notes: The sourcing run found eight qualified accounts here, the densest segment on the slate.

markets.name: Sovereign telecom partnerships

evidence.value: Bell AI Fabric runs North on Canadian infrastructure; TELUS, Swisscom, and Telefonica are building sovereign AI factories
Partner motion rather than end-customer motion: the ICP describes their customers, not them

markets.notes: Distribution rather than direct revenue; scores high on access precisely because it is a channel play.

markets.name: DACH regulated enterprise

evidence.value: Aleph Alpha merger provides a German footprint; SAP partnership for full-stack sovereign AI
EU data-sovereignty requirements are among the strictest in the world

markets.notes: The merger makes this newly enterable; timing is the argument for going now rather than later.

markets.name: Canadian healthcare and insurance

evidence.value: Insurer programs are live (Manulife, Intact); provider-side health systems are earlier and slower
Health data regimes are strict and vary by province

markets.notes: Perfect ICP fit, slower clock. The insurance half is already being worked inside financial services.

markets.name: US regulated enterprise

evidence.value: Azure OpenAI and Bedrock incumbency is strongest here, and their residency guarantees clear many US reviews
No sovereign-partner equivalent to the Bell or federal relationships

markets.notes: The biggest market and the worst fit for the wedge: this is where the category bet's falsifier lives.

markets.name: Mid-market SaaS

evidence.value: ICP disqualifier: comfortable on public APIs with no data constraint, so they default to OpenAI or Anthropic

markets.notes: On the slate deliberately, to make the disqualifier visible in the ranking rather than assumed.

markets.name: Japan enterprise

evidence.value: SoftBank and OpenAI launched SB OAI Japan, a 50-50 joint venture selling enterprise AI exclusively in Japan

markets.notes: Sovereignty demand is real and the market is ready, but the dominant channel is contracted to a competitor. Kept visible so the decision is explicit.
